title: Introduction to Neuroanatomy and Neurophysiology
description: This course is an introduction to the anatomy and physiology of the central and peripheral nervous systems. Related symptoms and pathologies are presented. This course is designed for students enrolled in the Neurodiagnostic Technology program.
outcomes: Introduction to the anatomy and physiology of the central and peripheral nervous systems. Related symptoms and pathologies are presented.
Students will be able to describe clinical conditions which affect the autonomic nervous system.
Students will be able to describe in detail how the pupils, sleep, and respiration are controlled by the central nervous system.
Students will be able to describe in detail how the pupils, sleep, and respiration are controlled by the central nervous system.
objectives: Compare and contrast the four supporting cell types found in the nervous system and their basic functions.
Diagram the electrophysiologic characteristics of the neuron relating it to the electrophysiology and generation of EEG activity and with typical neuromuscular activation.
Identify, describe and illustrate the vascular design of the nervous system including arterial supply and the venous/sinus system.
Discriminate the pattern of arterial supply to the major areas of the cerebrum.
Contrast the functional and anatomical differences between the sympathetic and parasympathetic control of the autonomic functions.
Describe the role of the hypothalamus in the autonomic nervous system.
Contrast the functional and anatomical differences of the anterior and posterior lobe of the pituitary gland.
Describe clinical conditions which affect the autonomic nervous system.
Know the order, major functions, and nuclei location of all 12 cranial nerves.
Identify, describe or illustrate the major peripheral nerves, and recall the functional characteristics and common clinical conditions associated with structures identified.
Identify the functional characteristics of the meningeal layers, their spaces and their functional characteristics.
Identify, describe or illustrate the ventricles of the brain and route of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), their functional characteristics and the formation and excretion of CSF.
Identify, describe or illustrate the major structures of the cerebrum including their functional characteristics: lobes, gyri, fissures, commissures and "deep" structures.
Compare and contrast the major functional aspects of the brainstem anatomy.
Illustrate the external aspect and sectional brainstem identifying the cranial nerves and key anatomy within the brainstem.
Describe clinical correlations affecting the brainstem and cranial nerves.
Describe neuroembryology and the clinical conditions which can affect the development of the nervous system.
Describe in detail how the pupils, sleep, and respiration are controlled by the central nervous system.

Identify, describe or illustrate the major structures of the visual and vestibulocochlear systems, and recall the functional characteristics and common clinical conditions associated with structures identified.
Describe the clinical conditions of the forms of epilepsy and seizures, hydrocephalus, meningitis, meningeal hemorrhage and cerebrovascular accident (stroke).
Describe the clinical conditions of meningitis and meningeal hemorrhage.
Describe the clinical correlation of cerebrovascular accident (CVA, stroke).
content: Electrophysiology and generation of EEG activity
Pituitary gland - anterior and posterior lobe function
Cranial nerves - nuclei location and nerve function
Major restructures including lobes, gyri, sulci, longitudinal fissure and deep structures (basal ganglia)
Functional characteristers of the major structures
Diencephalon including thalamus, hypothalamus and pineal gland
Brainstem including midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata
Microscopic anatomy, electrophysiology and electroencephalography generation
Neurologic exam, tests and history taking
assignments: Professional journals related to neurology and neurodiagnostic technology including: Journal of Clinical Neurophysiology and Neurodiagnostic Journal
Illustrating the vascular design of the nervous system including arterial supply.
Identifying the major function of the cranial nerves.
Detailing how the pupils, sleep and respiration are controlled by the central nervous system.
Identifying the major structures and their function of the visual and vestibulocochlear systems.
